account.fact: Dibsy: Dibsy supports hosted/API payments, merchant dashboard with refunds, team roles and settlement twice weekly; native merchant tools strong

triggers.quote: Dibsy's MCP roadmap will allow deeper AI-powered workflows across the payment lifecycle, including payment recovery, support automation, settlement visibility, reconciliation
triggers.summary: Dibsy launched AI Insights in the merchant dashboard; its roadmap covers payment recovery, settlement visibility and reconciliation.
triggers.ops_implication: They are building settlement and reconciliation tooling for merchants while volume grows fast.

triggers.quote: its transaction count rose by 49% compared with the same period a year earlier, while payment volume increased by 112%
triggers.summary: Dibsy entered the Forbes Middle East Fintech 50 for 2026; in Q1 2026 transactions grew 49% and payment volume 112% year over year.
triggers.ops_implication: More money rides on every refund or settlement case that goes wrong.

research.process_a: refunds that don't land and settlements that don't match
research.notes: They build similar merchant-facing tooling; angle is building on top instead of from scratch.

packages.ending_call: Would 20 minutes be worth it to compare build notes?

touches.subject: +112% volume
touches.body:
Hi Dinesh,

Congrats on the Forbes Fintech 50 and on Q1 volume up 112%.

AI Insights has been live since April, and reconciliation is next. My guess is building that in-house while volume doubles is a big project.

Each system owns only its piece. We've built software that holds the whole operation across them and shows why it's still open, with the evidence and an owner. The interesting part is what to build on top, and we'd rather shape it with a few payments teams on real data than guess.

For Dibsy, that could mean putting a month of settlements through it before committing engineers, and seeing which never closed.

Worth testing on settlements, or another part of the roadmap?

Ilia Frolov
CRO & Product Architect, HAIA
haia.finance

Dinesh, congrats on the Forbes Fintech 50 and on Q1 volume up 112%. AI Insights has been live since April, and reconciliation is next. Each system owns only its piece; we've built software that holds the whole operation and shows why it's still open. We're shaping what comes next with a few payments teams. Worth running a month of settlements through it before committing engineers, or is another part of the roadmap a better fit?

Ilia

Hi Dinesh,

Another angle: failed payments. Your guide to Qatar decline codes shows how much context a merchant needs to recover a payment.

Recovery is on your roadmap too. The same software could test a retry or recovery rule on a month of declines and show which payments it would have saved, before it goes live.

Is recovery a bigger lever than settlements for you right now?

Ilia

Dinesh, one question. With AI Insights already in merchants' hands, do you plan for the AI to act on settlement issues itself, or only flag them to a person? I'd value your view on where that line should sit. I emailed you a short note.

Ilia

Dinesh, closing the loop on my notes. If this sits with someone else at Dibsy, who would be best to talk to? Happy to take it from there.

Ilia
